text:
ryan.h: heads up — customer A reported a sharp p99 regression (~2x) on /v1/generate when using tool calls + structured_output schema. Started ~09:12 PDT. Full support ticket attached.
maya.s: got the ticket. request_id=rid_8a2f4. They included sample prompt + schema. p95 is fine, p99 is spiking to ~260-320ms on router/validator path (baseline ~120ms).
ops-bot: alert: service=tool-router env=prod metric=p99_latency_ms value=312 threshold=250 trigger_ts=1778501175
deploy-bot: recent rollout: eng-runtime/2026-03-15 02:30 UTC (small validator refactor) — potentially related.
ryan.h: repro steps from customer (condensed):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\
  -d '{"model":"open-lite-100b","input":"call weather_api","structured_output":true,"schema":{...},"tool_calls":[{"name":"weather_api","params":{"city":"sf"}}]}'
```
They run bursts of ~200 concurrent requests and see p99 climb only when schema present.
eli_k: quick datapoint from runtime traces — validation/serialization is the slow path. We compile JSON schema per-request in some cases; the recent refactor delayed caching of compiled validators for nested schemas, so heavy/complex schemas hit parse+compile on the hot path.
jordan_ml: can you paste the router trace snippet? I want to know split between: routing, schema-compile, validator-run, kv-cache lookup, model-invoke.
eli_k: snippet (trimmed):
```
route_start -> 0.8ms
compile_schema -> 95.4ms
validate_input -> 34.1ms
router_dispatch -> 4.3ms
model_invoke_pre -> 40.0ms
```
compile_schema accounts for the bulk of the extra ~80-160ms vs baseline.
maya.s: customer says schema is moderately complex (nested objects + oneOf + conditional). They cannot simplify right now.
ryan.h: immediate workaround offered to customer: add header `X-Redwood-Skip-Input-Validation: true` to bypass server-side JSON schema validation (we warned about safety). They accepted temporary bypass for now.
support-lead: note we should only recommend bypass when customer trusts model/tool inputs. Also track on their account to re-enable after fix.
eli_k: proposed quick fixes:
- enable compiled-schema cache keyed by schema-hash (should be safe) — low-effort
- increase validator worker pool size for dedicated validator CPU queue — immediate capacity mitigation
- background async-compile: accept request, run validation in background if schema seen before; for new schema compile async and fall back to sync for first few callers
jordan_ml: longer-term: implement a fast-path validator for our tool-router where we only do shallow validation for tool-routing (presence/type) and full schema validation later in post-processing. That would keep p99 low for routing.
maya.s: can eng-prod flip a flag to use cached compiled validators for this customer only? That would unblock them.
eli_k: yes. I can add a per-customer cache bypass toggle on runtime config. Rolling a canary in 10m.
ops-bot: note: canary config change requires config-service approval — pinging @eli_k in infra channel for rollout window.
eli_k: I'll coordinate with infra. For quick mitigation I'm going to bump validator-pool size from 6 -> 12 on the region serving this tenant; should reduce queueing for compile tasks.
maya.s: customer confirmed improved p99 to ~140ms after temporarily skipping validation header. They want ETA for permanent fix.
eli_k: ETA for compiled-schema cache patch + config flag = ~2d (dev + test + canary). Validator pool bump pushed now — monitoring.
ryan.h: action items tracked:
- ENG-Runtime (eli_k): implement schema-hash compiled cache + per-customer toggle (2d)
- ENG-Infrastructure: approve canary window + monitor config rollout (today)
- Support (maya.s): keep customer on bypass and collect perf curves until patched
- Product: prioritize fast-path shallow validation for router (roadmap)
support-lead: also add regression alerting to detect similar spikes when new schema patterns are introduced (schema complexity heuristic).
jordan_ml: one more note — if schema contains `oneOf` with many branches we should pre-flatten it into a union check that is faster; logging needed to detect bad patterns. Adding to ticket.
eli_k: temporary log command to surface heavy schemas in prod:
```
log.info('schema-heavy', { request_id, schema_hash, depth: calc_depth(schema), oneOf_count: countOneOf(schema), compile_time_ms })
```
maya.s: thanks. forwarding summary to customer. will keep thread updated.
ryan.h: thanks team. follow up tomorrow with post-mortem and metrics. :thumbsup:
